Product Overview Success Stories FAQ About Us

Product Overview

Zhenshili is a visual training tool designed for children with amblyopia: it breaks professional visual training into daily tasks that are easy for children to understand and complete, while automatically recording progress after each session. Parents can clearly see what was practiced each day and how the training is progressing. We also provide one-to-one support: professionals can help create a training plan based on the child’s examination results, answer questions, and continuously track training progress.

What does it do?

01
Clear Daily TasksThe app opens to the day’s “Today’s Training” plan, so children can immediately see what to practice and for how long. Parents do not need to reorganize the schedule every day.
02
Training RecordsEach session automatically records completion and duration. Parents can review the records at any time and use them with professionals during follow-up visits.
03
Designed for Home UseWorks on phones, tablets, and computers, allowing families to choose the device that fits their needs and complete training at home.

When might it be considered?

It is mainly intended for children who have received an ophthalmic examination, have no confirmed retinal or fundus disease, and have been assessed by a professional as suitable for visual training.

If a child is using corrective lenses, patching, or other visual-function training, Zhenshili can be used as a supporting daily training tool to help turn the training plan into a consistent routine.

Important:Software-based training cannot replace corrective lenses, patching, ophthalmic follow-up, or medical care. Whether to use it and how to schedule training should be determined according to the child’s condition and professional guidance.

Make Training Easier to Continue

Keep the day’s tasks in one place and reduce the burden on parents of reorganizing training every day.

Give Parents Better Visibility

Use training records to understand completion and support periodic review, rather than simply checking whether the software was opened.

Support Better Follow-Up

Training records can be shared with doctors or professionals alongside ophthalmic examination results for reference.

FAQ

What if my child does not want to practice?

First identify the reason: difficulty operating the software, tasks that are too hard, trouble maintaining attention, or discomfort after training. For younger children, parents are encouraged to stay with them and make training part of a fixed daily routine.

How long should training take each day?

The available materials suggest once a day for about 20 minutes per session. The exact frequency and duration should follow examination results, training items, and professional guidance; do not increase the schedule on your own.

What if discomfort occurs during training?

Pause the current training and record the task and time when the problem occurred. If discomfort is significant or persistent, stop training and consult an eye-care professional.

Can Zhenshili replace corrective lenses, patching, or follow-up visits?

No. Zhenshili is a visual training tool and cannot replace corrective lenses, patching, ophthalmic follow-up, or medical diagnosis and treatment.
